_comment: Source of the historical cards and portals. Edit here, then run `npm run media` (scripts/build_media.py): it verifies each person's office on the date against Wikidata, fetches portraits and city photos from Wikimedia Commons with their licenses, and writes public/data/history-content.json and docs/history-verification.md. People whose office cannot be verified are left out of the app.

events.title: The dollar-gold break
events.summary: On 15 August 1971 the United States stopped converting dollars into gold for foreign governments. Within days most major currencies began to move against the dollar; Japan let the yen float from 28 August.
policies: Suspension of the dollar's convertibility into gold
A 90-day freeze on wages and prices

people.involvement: Announced the measures in a televised address on 15 August 1971.
Led the US side in the currency talks that followed, which ended in the Smithsonian Agreement of December 1971.
Took part in the Camp David meetings of 13 to 15 August 1971 at which the measures were prepared.
His government kept the yen at 360 per dollar for about two weeks, then let it float on 28 August 1971.

events.title: A coordinated push on the dollar

where.note: The agreement was made at a meeting in New York.

events.summary: On 22 September 1985 the finance ministers and central bank governors of five major economies met in New York and said a further orderly rise of other currencies against the dollar was desirable. The dollar's fall that followed is widely associated with the agreement, although the dollar had already peaked in early 1985.
policies: Joint statement of the G5: United States, Japan, West Germany, France and the United Kingdom

people.involvement: Hosted the meeting of the five countries in New York.
Attended as head of the US central bank.

people.role: Governor of the Bank of Japan
people.roleMatch: Governor of the Bank of Japan
people.involvement: Attended for the Bank of Japan.
Represented West Germany at the meeting.

events.title: The Asian currency crisis
events.summary: From July 1997 several Asian currencies fell sharply as foreign capital left the region. South Korea asked the IMF for support on 21 November 1997 and a rescue program was agreed on 3 December. Between June and late December the won fell from about 888 to about 1,743 per dollar.
policies: IMF stand-by arrangement for Korea, approved on 4 December 1997
Higher interest rates and restructuring of the financial sector under the program
The won's daily trading band was widened in November and removed in December 1997

people.involvement: In office when Korea requested and agreed the IMF program.

people.role: Minister of Finance and Economy of South Korea
people.involvement: Announced on 21 November 1997 that Korea would ask the IMF for support.

people.role: Governor of the Bank of Korea
people.involvement: Headed the central bank during the crisis.
Headed the IMF, whose board approved the program for Korea on 4 December 1997.

events.title: The global financial crisis
events.summary: In September and October 2008 a banking crisis that began in the United States spread around the world. Investors moved into the dollar and the yen: between late June and late November the won fell from about 1,040 to about 1,470 per dollar, and the Australian dollar lost about a third of its value against the dollar.
policies: Troubled Asset Relief Program, enacted on 3 October 2008
Coordinated interest-rate cut by six central banks on 8 October 2008
Dollar swap lines from the Federal Reserve to other central banks, including the Bank of Korea on 29 October 2008
Bank of Japan rate cut to 0.3% on 31 October 2008

people.involvement: Signed the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act, which created the Troubled Asset Relief Program, on 3 October 2008.
Proposed the 700-billion-dollar rescue program to Congress in September 2008.
The Federal Reserve joined the coordinated rate cut of 8 October and extended dollar swap lines to other central banks.
